projects.title: NeuroScan AI — Brain Tumor Detection & Explainability
projects.problem: Brain tumors—including infiltrative Gliomas, dural-based Meningiomas, and sellar Pituitary adenomas—are critical intracranial pathologies requiring rapid, accurate radiological evaluation. While Convolutional Neural Networks achieve impressive diagnostic accuracy, their black-box nature creates a barrier to clinical adoption because clinicians cannot trust predictions without understanding where the algorithm is focusing.
projects.solution: Built an end-to-end clinical deep learning system for 4-class intracranial tumor diagnosis from cranial MRI scans. Powered by a MobileNetV2 transfer-learning classifier with 86.12% test accuracy (99.0% healthy recall), integrated with mathematical Grad-CAM visual heatmaps that localize the lesion bed without requiring pixel-level annotation masks, and served through a real-time Streamlit diagnostic studio.
workflow: Curated and validated a clinical dataset of 7,200 brain MRI slices divided across 4 classes (Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary Adenoma, and Healthy Brain), maintaining an untouched 1,600-scan benchmark test set.
Engineered an anatomically safe data augmentation pipeline (RandomFlip, 5% rotation, 5% zoom) and scaled pixel intensities to [-1, 1] matching MobileNetV2 preprocessing standards.

Constructed a transfer learning architecture with a frozen ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 base, tapping the final 'out_relu' layer (7x7x1280), followed by GlobalAveragePooling2D, BatchNormalization, and Dropout regularization heads.

Implemented mathematical Grad-CAM extracting class-specific gradients with respect to 'out_relu' feature maps, passing through ReLU to isolate positive tumor activations and superimposing Jet heatmaps onto grayscale MRIs (α=0.45).

Engineered a production-ready Streamlit Diagnostic Studio featuring sub-second model caching (@st.cache_resource), dual scan input (custom MRI slice upload or pre-loaded test cases), multi-class probability breakdown, and side-by-side saliency comparisons.
features: 4-Class Intracranial Classification: Accurately differentiates between Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary Adenoma, and Healthy Brain (No Tumor).
High Clinical Sensitivity: Achieves 99.0% recall on healthy brain scans and virtually 0% false negative rate for tumor presence.
Zero-Annotation Tumor Localization: Generates spatial Grad-CAM heatmaps pinpointing lesion beds without requiring expensive pixel-level segmentation masks.
Empirical Performance Gain: Retrained on full clinical data to elevate test accuracy from 82.19% baseline to 86.12% (+3.93%) with -0.0885 categorical loss reduction.
Interactive Diagnostic Studio: Streamlit web dashboard with instant MRI inference, probability bars, pure heatmaps, and side-by-side radiological overlays.
challenges: Resolving visual ambiguity between infiltrative intra-axial gliomas and well-circumscribed extra-axial meningiomas without spatial segmentation masks.
Eliminating false alarms on healthy intracranial scans while ensuring high sensitivity (99.25% recall) for deep skull base pituitary lesions.
futureImprovements: Extending classification to 3D volumetric MRI scans (NIfTI / multi-slice axial sequences).
Integrating automated radiological impression reporting using multimodal Vision-Language Models (VLMs).

projects.title: YouTube Video RAG Chatbot
projects.problem: Extracting key insights or getting specific answers from long video lectures and tutorials is time-consuming and inefficient.
projects.solution: Built a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) based Question Answering system that extracts YouTube transcripts, creates vector indices, and feeds relevant video context to Google's Gemini model to produce highly accurate, context-bound responses.
workflow: Engineered a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using LangChain, FAISS, HuggingFace Embeddings, and Gemini AI to support context-aware question answering.
Performed data collection and preprocessing of YouTube transcripts, generating vector embeddings and implementing semantic search for accurate information retrieval.
Integrated retrieval and LLM-based generation techniques to deliver reliable, context-relevant responses, improving insight extraction from unstructured data.
features: Direct transcript download using only a YouTube Video ID.
Dense vector semantic search capable of handling conceptual questions.
Modular chain pipeline using LangChain and FAISS vector indexing.
challenges: Handling transcripts with variable formatting and multi-speaker segments.
Tuning chunk size and embeddings to balance context recall with latency.
futureImprovements: Adding interactive UI with source timestamp citations.
Multi-turn conversation memory for continuous Q&A.

projects.title: Movie Recommendation System
projects.problem: With thousands of movies available online, users struggle to find relevant titles that match their specific tastes, leading to choice paralysis.
projects.solution: Built a content-based machine learning recommendation model using cosine similarity and feature engineering on the TMDb movie dataset, deployed via an interactive Streamlit UI.
workflow: Built a content-based machine learning recommendation model using cosine similarity and feature engineering on the TMDb movie dataset.
Conducted exploratory data analysis (EDA) and data cleaning on movie metadata to identify patterns and improve recommendation accuracy.
Developed an interactive Streamlit application integrated with the TMDb API for dynamic data retrieval and presentation.
features: Interactive movie selection interface with instant similarity ranking.
Dynamic poster visualization using live TMDb API queries.
Robust data cleaning and metadata preprocessing pipeline.
Fast content-based matching using cosine similarity.
challenges: Handling nested, dirty, string-formatted JSON data inside TMDB columns.
Optimizing similarity computation across large feature matrices.
futureImprovements: Hybrid recommendation combining content-based and collaborative filtering.
User rating feedback loop for personalized score adjustments.
